newsitem.title: POLAND: New job offers push Polish May unemployment down.
newsitem.headline: New job offers push Polish May unemployment down.

text.p: New job offers and stricter verification of jobless pushed Poland's unemployment rate down in May to 11.7 percent from 12.4 percent in April, Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski said on Friday.
"It (the unemployment fall) was mainly caused by an increase of new jobs, an advantageous situation on the labour market," Zielinski told a news conference.
"Registers at the labour offices have also been brought closer to reality. Our controls have eliminated part of those collecting unemployment benefits illegally," he added.
The number of unemployed dropped to 2.04 million in May from 2.13 million in April and 2.57 million in May last year. It was the third consecutive monthly fall.
The number of vacancies was 88,800 in May, compared with 104,300 in April.
Zlielinski said the unemployment rate was likely to go up in June, when many graduates would register as jobless.
